There's Only One Snoop Dogg
Growing up in the late ‘90s and early 2000s, when hip-hop was becoming such a dominant force in mainstream music, there were a few names that introduced me to the genre, and Snoop was one of them. Charismatic, distinctive and, well, just Snoop Dogg. He’s definitely a character, and I think that’s a huge part of what has made him such a recognizable figure over the years.
Musically, “Doggystyle” remains the absolute pinnacle of his career for me, and it’s quite fascinating that he achieved that with his debut. Nothing that followed came particularly close, despite some glimpses of brilliance and a return to form with “Tha Blue Carpet Treatment”. One thing I’ve come to realize after spending around a year exploring his discography is that Snoop is more of a singles artist than an album artist. Even on some of his weakest records, there are songs that most of us have probably heard at some point in our lives, and that certainly counts for something.
I don’t want to end this journey on a negative note. As frustrating as it was at times, I’ll take the highs, that incredible debut and all those memorable songs that made him a household name. Having the opportunity to see him perform those songs live in Copenhagen a couple of years ago was something my younger self could only dream of and something my older self genuinely appreciated. Not the most consistent artist when it comes to albums, but certainly one of a kind in the rap industry. There’s only one Snoop Dogg.

Georgia: a song about yet another one of Phoebe’s relationships, Georgia focuses on a time when Phoebe was much younger and, according to genius, dating a boy from Georgia (hence the name). The song explores wanting validation from another. The song explores more common themes, like supporting another while they are going through mental health struggles and destructive behavior. Phoebe seems to question every action she does, whether it helps him or not “if I fix you, will you hate me”. I really do like this song, not particularly memorable to me and I wouldn’t play it all the time, but it is certainly very well crafted.
